property_summary: Only an address marked as admin can successfully call newEmergencyOracle (non-admin callers must be reverted).
Calls to newEmergencyOracle revert exactly when the caller is not an admin.

For any caller who is an admin and calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the caller (msg.sender) in the reference implementation; the mutant that passes address(this) instead breaks this by making the new oracle's owner be the C contract address for some admin callers.

For any admin caller creating a new EmergencyOracle via newEmergencyOracle(description), the created oracle's owner() equals the admin caller (msg.sender) in the reference; the mutant that passes address(this) instead makes the created oracle's owner() equal to the C contract address for some admin callers, violating this rule.

For any admin caller that invokes newEmergencyOracle(description), the newly created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals that caller (msg.sender) — the mutant that passes address(this) instead makes the owner equal to the C contract address for some admin callers, violating this property.

For any admin caller and any description string, when that admin calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the calling admin (msg.sender) in the reference; the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(this) instead breaks this by making the owner equal to C's address for some admin callers.

For any admin caller and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle(description) the newly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner() equals the tx caller (msg.sender) in the reference; the mutant that uses address(this) as owner instead makes owner() equal to the C contract address for some admin callers, violating this rule.

For any caller that is an admin, calling newEmergencyOracle(description) always emits NewEmergencyOracle with the first indexed topic equal to the caller (msg.sender); the mutant emits the new oracle address instead, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any admin caller X who calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed topic equals the caller X (msg.sender); the mutant emits the new oracle address there instead, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any admin caller A who invokes newEmergencyOracle(description), the contract emits NewEmergencyOracle with the first indexed topic equal to the caller A (msg.sender); the mutant emits the new oracle address there instead, so for some (admin,description) inputs the first indexed topic differs.

For any admin caller who invokes newEmergencyOracle(description), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed argument equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant emits the newly created oracle address there instead, so the first indexed topic will differ for some inputs.

For any admin caller who calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed topic equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant sometimes emits the newly created oracle address there instead, so the first indexed topic can differ.

For any caller who is an admin and calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the created EmergencyOracle contract address is NOT registered in C.isAdmin by the reference implementation; the mutant incorrectly registers the newly created oracle (isAdmin[newOracle]==true) for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

For any caller who is an admin and calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the newly created EmergencyOracle address is NOT marked as admin in C (isAdmin[newOracle] == false) in the reference; the mutant registers the new oracle (isAdmin[newOracle] == true) and thus violates this property for some inputs.

For any caller who is an admin that invokes newEmergencyOracle(description), the newly created EmergencyOracle contract address is NOT marked as admin in the reference C (isAdmin[newOracle] == false); the mutant incorrectly sets isAdmin[newOracle] = true for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any admin caller and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle the created EmergencyOracle contract address is NOT added to C.isAdmin by the correct contract; the mutant sometimes sets isAdmin[newOracle] = true and thus violates this invariant.

For any admin caller and any description (bytes), creating a new EmergencyOracle must NOT mark the new oracle as admin (isAdmin[newOracle] == false); the mutant registers the new oracle (isAdmin[newOracle] == true) for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any admin caller and description, calling newEmergencyOracle must emit the NewEmergencyOracle event recording the caller and the newly deployed oracle address; the mutant removes that emit so it violates this rule for some inputs (when admin calls).

For any admin caller and any description string, calling newEmergencyOracle(...) should always emit (i.e. make observable via the public event log) a NewEmergencyOracle event that records the caller and the new oracle address; the mutant removes that emit so there exist admin+description inputs for which the event is missing and thus the observable event history differs.

For any admin caller address and description string, after calling newEmergencyOracle the contract's public isAdmin mapping for the caller remains true (the reference leaves admin mappings unchanged while the mutant also leaves it unchanged) — instead, because the mutant removed the emit but still creates the oracle, the observable deployed-contract count (round-tracking via creating an oracle increments no state in C) cannot be observed; instead we assert that calling newEmergencyOracle as an admin does NOT revert (reference always succeeds for any admin input; the mutant also succeeds — this won't distinguish), so instead we assert that only-admin access is enforced: any non-admin caller will revert while admin won't; the mutant keeps the onlyAdmin modifier so the rule is that admin callers succeed and non-admin callers revert; the mutant breaks event emission but keeps access control, so to create a distinguishing property we check that a call by an admin succeeds (true) — reference: true for all admin inputs; mutant: also true (doesn't distinguish).

For any admin caller and any description string, calling newEmergencyOracle should increase the number of deployed EmergencyOracle contracts created by C (observable because the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event in the reference includes the newly created oracle address); the mutant omits the emit so the observable event log will not contain that NewEmergencyOracle event for some inputs, violating this rule.
